about.title: Two siblings, one counter and a lot of coffee.
about.intro: Café Palanca opened in 2024 on a quiet street in Luanda, because Domingas and Tomás wanted a place where everyone feels at home.

blocks.title: Tomás went to the source for the beans
blocks.text: Her younger brother Tomás spent two years in Amboim, in Kwanza Sul, learning from families who have grown coffee for generations. Today he chooses the beans with them directly and roasts in small batches on Tuesday and Thursday mornings.
blocks.alt: Freshly roasted coffee beans tumbling out of a roaster.

blocks.title: Domingas learned to make coffee in Lisbon
blocks.text: Domingas Kiala grew up in Luanda and went to study in Lisbon at 19. She paid her way working at a small roastery, where she learned that a good espresso takes patience. She came back in 2022 with a second-hand machine and one idea: to serve the coffee she loved to drink in Luanda.
blocks.alt: A barista in an apron holding a cup of coffee.

blocks.title: Dona Rosa runs the bakery
blocks.text: The carrot cake and custard tart recipes are their mother's, Dona Rosa. She still turns up at the counter on Saturdays to taste everything and tell them, without ceremony, what could be better.
blocks.alt: A bakery display with pastries and bread fresh from the oven.

counter.alt: The café counter, with an espresso machine and wooden shelves.

palanca.title: Why Palanca?
palanca.text: The sable antelope, the palanca negra, is a symbol of Angola. It has roots here and goes its own way, horns held high. That's how we want to serve coffee: proud of what's ours, with the door open to whoever walks in.

cta.title: Drop in
cta.text: There's always a free table and a cup warming.
